meta.title: Per-User MCP Access via In-Chat Connect  [PROPOSED]
meta.subtitle: Channel user hits a per_user MCP (Jira/GitHub/Workday) → reply with a signed connect link → OAuth → persist → act as the user. Not in current docs.

segments.label: Now connected — act as the user

messages.label: vault + persist (subject, server)
messages.note: per-user DEK · reused across sessions + channels + console

cards.title: The idea — in-chat connect = login in-session
items: A channel user hits a per_user MCP tool they haven't connected → the agent replies with a signed OAuth connect link
They authorize in the browser (a normal web OAuth to api — out-of-band from chat), like logging in within that session
The run fails closed until connected; v1 the user re-asks, v2 the paused run resumes (like the tool-approval interrupt)

cards.title: Persisted per user, reused everywhere
items: mcp_user_connections keyed (workspace_id, user_subject, mcp_server_id) — connect once, reused across future sessions, other channels AND the console
The token is vaulted (per-user DEK), refreshed automatically, revoked on offboarding
This is the 'user-specific MCP json' persisted so later sessions skip the connect step

cards.title: Signed link = the trust boundary
items: The connect link carries a short-lived signed state (subject + server + workspace) so the OAuth callback binds to the right identity (anti-CSRF / anti-mix-up)
OAuth runs browser → api, never through the chat transport
Shared_service mode stays the default for read-only / eval-safe tools; per_user is opt-in per MCP server

cards.title: Act as the user (least privilege)
items: The MCP call runs in the sandbox with the user's own token → their downstream permissions + a real audit trail in Jira/GitHub/Workday
Egress allow-list still applies; the MCP server's declared scopes bound what the token can do
Channel federation already carries the Okta subject — where the IdP supports it (Entra OBO), the connect step can be skipped via true token exchange

cards.title: Status: PROPOSED — delta vs current design
items: Not in docs/backend today: MCP creds are workspace-level + shared; access_policy only gates visibility
Needs: mcp_servers.auth_mode ∈ {shared_service, per_user} · mcp_user_connections table · an OAuth connect/callback route
Caveat: eval has no real user → per_user tools use a designated service connection or are excluded from scoring (not deterministically evaluable)
